subject.title: macOS update can leave manual-update loop and stale node host causing Gateway restart storm

question: Should same-version package updates on macOS managed installs exit before service stop/restart, or should OpenClaw keep refreshing the package and add stronger dedupe/recovery around that behavior?
rationale: The stale-label gap is mechanically clear, but no-op update semantics versus intentional package refresh is a user-visible managed-install policy choice.

options.title: No-op same-version package updates
options.body: Exit before package refresh and managed service restart when the installed package already matches the target version and no channel or config change requires mutation.

options.title: Refresh with dedupe and recovery
options.body: Keep same-version package refresh behavior but add per-install update locking, stale job cleanup, node-host restart, and launchd health verification before success.

options.title: Docs-only for now
options.body: Document detection and manual recovery while accepting continued manual intervention for some macOS update loops.

recommendation.title: No-op same-version package updates
recommendation.body: Exit before package refresh and managed service restart when the installed package already matches the target version and no channel or config change requires mutation.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent current-line history and PR 88764 co-authorship put this account closest to the update lifecycle policy decision.
